motions.purpose: Separates a body into its parts without hiding what is attached to what. The direction is not a scatter: each part withdraws from the part it MOUNTS TO, along the reverse of its assembly direction. Parts travelling the same way are packed by their projection along that direction so none overtakes another. On top of that the transition carries three readings: parts leave in DISASSEMBLY ORDER (outermost first, via a per-part stagger), each one takes a small separation ATTITUDE as it withdraws and returns to its declared attitude exactly as it arrives, and brightness tracks each part's own SPEED so the eye can follow what is moving.
motions.pauseControl: The explode slider is scrubbable at any time and k is a position, not a playback: scrubbing back retraces exactly. Playback pauses; any step can be jumped to; the mode (assembly / axial / radial / layered) switches live; section cuts; the turntable toggles. Dragging orbits, the wheel zooms.
motions.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the stagger and the separation attitude are switched OFF (spread = 0, amplitude = 0), the glint and the selection pulse are off, the turntable never starts, and the slider is applied instantly. The resulting state is bit-identical to the animated endpoint - validate-exploded-motion.mjs proves that rather than assuming it. Nothing is lost except the transit.
motions.exportState: ?object=satellite|habitat|rover|lander|rocket|orbiter selects the body. Default satellite. Explode ratio, mode and step are set on screen.
motions.accessibility: Controls are native form elements with a measured target size of 44 px or more. Labels never sit on the body: they go to two balanced gutters, are packed by their MEASURED height, and each is tied to its part by a numbered balloon and a leader with a shoulder. Below 560 px of stage width the layer switches to compact - fewer labels, name only - because a label that cannot be read is worse than no label. Estimated masses and inferred interfaces are marked in text, not by colour alone. Hover is a steady highlight and selection is a pulse, so the two never look alike.
motions.limitations: Two paths with DIFFERENT truth levels sit side by side. For declared bodies (satellite, surface base) mass, interface and assembly order come from a catalogue. For derived bodies (rover, lander, launch vehicle, orbiter) the tree is read off the scene graph, mass is ESTIMATED from bounding volume and the interface is inferred from node names: those absolute numbers are not meaningful, only their rough proportions, and the interface says so. The separation attitude is a READING AID, not dynamics: these parts are not falling, thrusting or floating in a current, and no part is simulated. Collision packing keeps parts from overtaking one another along a shared direction, but it is not a general collision check and parts on different directions can still visually overlap from some camera angles. The section is a single plane.
motions.notes: Core: presets/core/assembly.mjs holds WHERE parts go and never imports three, so every explosion decision is verifiable without a screen (scripts/validate-assembly.mjs, 52 checks). presets/core/exploded-motion.mjs holds HOW they get there and is likewise pure - stagger, smootherstep easing, separation attitude, speed and the selection pulse are all closed forms of (k, part) with no integrator and no per-frame state (scripts/validate-exploded-motion.mjs, 33 checks, including the property the whole feature rests on: the attitude returns to zero at both ends to within 3e-17 rad). presets/core/exploded-view.mjs applies both to the scene. Adapters: adapters/catalog.mjs for declared catalogues (the satellite and the surface base share one shape), adapters/scene.mjs for ANY three object. Determinism: per-part variation comes from a hashed id, never Math.random; the hash carries a MurmurHash3 finalizer because FNV-1a alone put similar ids within 0.01 of each other (chi-square 128.9 against a 1% threshold of 21.67; now 8.0).
